claims.text: Systematically changing elemental ratios in a non-equiatomic HEA can tune its magnetic ordering temperatures.
Reducing strongly magnetic elements or adding a weakly magnetic element can tune the magnetocaloric response.
Composition changes tune magnetic behavior by modifying exchange interactions and magnetic anisotropy.
The initial alloy is a random solid solution.
The initial alloy has predominantly magnetic elements in near-equiatomic ratios.
Decreasing the concentration of strongly magnetic elements or incorporating a weakly magnetic element will reduce saturation magnetization.
The proposed behavior applies to low-dimensional specimens such as thin films or micropatterned structures.
Controlled thermal processing can preserve a single-phase structure during the proposed compositional tuning.
A non-equiatomic elemental distribution induces local chemical disorder and lattice distortions.
Reducing the concentration of strongly magnetic atoms alters exchange coupling.
Reducing the concentration of strongly magnetic atoms lowers saturation magnetization.
Reducing the concentration of strongly magnetic atoms modifies magnetocrystalline anisotropy.
Changes in exchange coupling and anisotropy shift Curie temperatures and alter the sharpness of magnetic transitions.
The FeCoNiTi evidence system exhibits multiple phase-associated ferromagnetic transitions.
Magnetic transition temperature and transition sharpness are critical determinants of the magnetocaloric effect.
The intervention will decrease saturation magnetization and systematically shift magnetic ordering temperatures.
The intervention will enhance or enable targeting of the magnetocaloric entropy change while maintaining a single-phase HEA.
Excessive compositional deviation may induce secondary phases or degrade magnetic entropy change if the magnetic moment becomes too small.
Ti is a weakly magnetic substituent suitable for the proposed composition series.
